hypotheses.reasoning: notification-svc's messageCache keeps growing until the heap runs out. At 14:23:36, after a full GC, the heap was still 78% used with the old generation not reclaimed (#2805). The heap then ran out while growing messageCache at 14:28:00 (#3834), and the OOM killer took the pod (#3837). It happened again at 14:30:56 (#4210, #4212) and 14:34:11 (#4626, #4629). Every restart runs the same v4.16.1 and starts by warming the message cache, so notification-svc was not redeployed. Each crash and restart leaves no healthy upstream, and the gateway's 502 'connection reset (no healthy upstream)' errors on POST /v1/notify start at 14:28:43, right after the first OOM. That explains why the 502s come in bursts. Ruled out as unrelated: report-cron failing on a missing pandas module, account-svc/accounts-db errors on a missing status_v2 column (they only affect /login), status-poller timing out against a deprecated endpoint, and the notif-worker v1.2.6 deploy at 14:25:48, which came after the heap was already in trouble at 14:23:36.

notif-worker v1.2.6 rolled out at 14:25:48, shortly before the first OOM. It could in theory have changed message traffic into notification-svc. But the heap was already under pressure before the rollout, and notif-worker kept processing batches normally afterwards.
Queries fail because the status_v2 column is missing from accounts, which suggests a half-applied migration. This only affects account-svc and /login, not /v1/notify.

verdict.recommendedAction: Raise notification-svc's memory/heap limits for now, or cap messageCache (size limit or eviction/TTL), so the pods stop crash-looping. Analyze /tmp/heap.hprof to find the unbounded growth in messageCache and fix it. Track the accounts status_v2 migration and the report-cron missing pandas module as separate issues.

hypotheses.reasoning: notification-svc's messageCache keeps growing until the heap runs out. At 14:23:36, after a full GC, the heap was still 78% used with the old generation not reclaimed (#2805). The heap then ran out while growing messageCache at 14:28:00 (#3834), and the OOM killer took the pod (#3837). It happened again at 14:30:56 (#4210, #4212) and 14:34:11 (#4626, #4629). Every restart runs the same v4.16.1 and starts by warming the message cache, so notification-svc was not redeployed. Each crash and restart leaves no healthy upstream, and the gateway's 502 'connection reset (no healthy upstream)' errors on POST /v1/notify start at 14:28:43, right after the first OOM. That explains why the 502s come in bursts. Ruled out as unrelated: report-cron failing on a missing pandas module, account-svc/accounts-db errors on a missing status_v2 column (they only affect /login), status-poller timing out against a deprecated endpoint, and the notif-worker v1.2.6 deploy at 14:25:48, which came after the heap was already in trouble at 14:23:36.

notif-worker v1.2.6 rolled out at 14:25:48, shortly before the first OOM. It could in theory have changed message traffic into notification-svc. But the heap was already under pressure before the rollout, and notif-worker kept processing batches normally afterwards.
Queries fail because the status_v2 column is missing from accounts, which suggests a half-applied migration. This only affects account-svc and /login, not /v1/notify.

input.recommendedAction: Raise notification-svc's memory/heap limits for now, or cap messageCache (size limit or eviction/TTL), so the pods stop crash-looping. Analyze /tmp/heap.hprof to find the unbounded growth in messageCache and fix it. Track the accounts status_v2 migration and the report-cron missing pandas module as separate issues.
